findings.description: Task 5.7 migrates langfuse_env.sh to isolated internal credential inputs and CFG-19 says the internal loader SHALL use only the internal credential inputs, yet the helper still prefers a raw BAO_TOKEN over BAO_INTERNAL_ROLE_ID/BAO_INTERNAL_SECRET_ID. The new .secrets.yaml.example labels BAO_TOKEN 'Provisioning only; never dispatch', so an operator shell that still exports the provisioning token after a seeding run will have the Langfuse helper silently read secret/coordinator with provisioner privileges instead of the isolated AppRole. The Python internal loader (agent-coordinator/src/config.py:275-300) accepts only the internal AppRole inputs, so the two internal consumers now have different credential contracts. The live test masks this by explicitly setting BAO_TOKEN='' (test_live_openbao.py:222). Either drop BAO_TOKEN precedence from the helper or document it as an intentional operator escape hatch and add a test that a set BAO_TOKEN with internal inputs present uses the AppRole.
findings.resolution: Remove the BAO_TOKEN branch (or make internal AppRole inputs win when present) and add a test_langfuse_env.py case asserting that BAO_TOKEN alone does not authenticate when internal inputs are configured; update the header comment.

findings.existing_code:
# Both are OPTIONAL. When unset, the identity map and the accepted-key allowlist are
# derived from agents.yaml — the registry is the single source of truth for agent
# identity and trust (see "Registry-derived identity" below). Setting the vars
# explicitly still overrides the registry, which is also the rollback lever.
findings.description: Task 5.5 explicitly requires that 'the old static-identity override is no longer presented as an OpenBao-mode rollback lever', and the new paragraph added at agent-coordinator/CLAUDE.md:5-12 says OpenBao mode 'does not accept a ... static API-key override'. The same file, which is inside wp-integration's write scope, still tells operators at line 229 that setting COORDINATION_API_KEYS 'overrides the registry, which is also the rollback lever' with no non-Bao-mode qualifier. Design D4 states that in configured Bao mode the static list cannot authorize an unbound or rotated key (COORD-09). An operator following the environment-variable block during an incident will reach for a lever that fails closed.
findings.resolution: Qualify the sentence: the static override applies only when BAO_ADDR is unset; in OpenBao mode the snapshot is the sole allowlist and rollback is the prior release plus the secret/coordinator backup (link to docs/openbao-secret-management.md).

findings.description: Task 5.3 lists CFG-17 ('sequential or concurrent dispatch processes ... only one process SHALL unwrap the one-use bundle') and design D3 states 'Tests cover sequential and simultaneous dispatch processes'. The live matrix only proves sequential reuse in a single process (this line), and the unit suite's test_session_renews_under_lock (packages/openbao-credentials/tests/test_adapter.py:202) also runs one process against a fake client. No test anywhere in the repo spawns two processes contending on <role>.lock against a fresh one-use bundle, so the flock serialization and 'second process reuses the token, not the consumed bundle' guarantee is unverified against a real server. Because the SecretID is secret_id_num_uses=1, a lock regression would surface only as intermittent AUTHENTICATION_FAILED in production.
findings.resolution: Add a live test that writes a fresh bundle, launches N subprocesses (multiprocessing or subprocess) that each call ensure_session concurrently, and asserts all return the same client_token, the bundle digest is recorded once, and sys/wrapping/lookup on the wrap token now fails (consumed once).

findings.existing_code:
for _ in range(3):
            time.sleep(2.0)
            renewed = _reader(live, role_name).ensure_session(principal_id, role_name)
            assert renewed.client_token == initial.client_token
            assert renewed.lease_expires_at > initial.lease_expires_at
findings.description: The periodic-renewal proof compares each iteration's lease_expires_at to the original session rather than to the previous iteration. After the first renewal at ~2s the inequality is satisfied for iterations two and three even if renewal stops, so the validation report's claim of 'three renewals over six seconds' is not what the loop asserts. The final read past the 5s mount max TTL (lines 283-285) does catch a stalled renewal in most timings via local lease expiry, but only indirectly and only if the wall clock has crossed the stored lease_expires_at; a stall on the second renewal with a slightly early third call would pass.
findings.resolution: Track `previous = initial` and assert `renewed.lease_expires_at > previous.lease_expires_at` then set `previous = renewed`; optionally also assert `time.monotonic() - start > 5` before the final read so the past-mount-max claim is explicit.

        assert runtime.lookup("alice-rotated") is not None
    finally:

findings.description: Task 5.4 claims COORD-05 ('a complete valid refresh succeeds ... restore ready identity status, and audit recovery') and COORD-09 (static allowlist cannot bypass rotation). The live rotation test ends in the degraded state; the finally block restores the documents but never calls reload() again to assert readiness returns to ('ready', True) and that the old rotated key stays denied. COORD-09 is not exercised live either: IdentityRuntime is constructed without required_static_keys. The unit suite (agent-coordinator/tests/test_openbao_identity.py) covers preflight blockers and grace expiry but has no named recovery test, so COORD-05 recovery against real Bao reads is unasserted.
findings.resolution: After restoring bob's document inside the try body, assert `runtime.reload()` is True, `runtime.readiness() == ('ready', True)`, and `runtime.lookup('alice-secret') is None`; construct the runtime with required_static_keys=('alice-secret',) once and assert the stale key appears in preflight_blockers after rotation.

findings.existing_code: **Authentication**: prefers `BAO_TOKEN` if set, otherwise uses AppRole login via `BAO_ROLE_ID` + `BAO_SECRET_ID` (matches `bao_seed.py`).
findings.description: The canonical skill document for langfuse_env.sh still tells agents and operators to authenticate the helper with BAO_ROLE_ID + BAO_SECRET_ID, which task 5.7 just removed from the script; test_legacy_approle_inputs_cannot_authenticate now proves those inputs are ignored. install.sh copies this file into .claude/skills and .agents/skills, so every harness will read stale guidance. The file is outside wp-integration's write_allow, so this needs a scope decision rather than an in-package edit.
findings.resolution: Either extend the package scope to skills/bao-vault/SKILL.md or file a follow-up to replace the sentence with BAO_INTERNAL_ROLE_ID + BAO_INTERNAL_SECRET_ID and note that BAO_TOKEN is provisioning-only.

findings.description: _reader accepts role_name but never uses it; every call site passes a role that is silently dropped, which reads as if the client were principal-scoped when in fact scoping happens later in ensure_session. Minor, but it misleads anyone extending the matrix.
findings.resolution: Drop the parameter (and the argument at all call sites) or use it to derive the expected bootstrap paths for an assertion.

findings.description: The immutable digest is stored twice (runner and docker-compose.yml) and the guard fails loudly on mismatch, which satisfies CFG-15. Two consequences worth recording: the `*':latest'` clause is unreachable once equality with a digest string is required, and .github/dependabot.yml has no docker-compose ecosystem entry, so the pinned image will never receive automated bump PRs; every OpenBao upgrade is a manual two-file edit. Acceptable for a pinned conformance fixture, but the upgrade path should be written down.
findings.resolution: Optionally read the digest from the Compose file as the single source and only reject non-digest references, and add a one-line 'to upgrade OpenBao' note in docs/openbao-secret-management.md.

findings.description: Test isolation is per-fixture (fresh reconciliation and 0700 directory per test after f5c50e86) but the OpenBao server is shared for the whole run, and two tests leave unmanaged server state behind: the Langfuse test creates role coordinator-internal plus policy coordinator-internal-read (lines 209-212) and the renewal test creates role agent-renewal bound to the agent-alice policy with no cleanup. The seeder's retirement check refuses unknown roles still holding coordinator-read (bao_seed.py:292), so the current seven tests pass in file order, but any future test that runs a --confirm-cutover reconciliation or that pytest reorders will inherit these roles. No secret material leaks: all values are synthetic and the test asserts the legacy inputs never reach stdout/stderr.
findings.resolution: Delete the ad-hoc role and policy in each test's finally block, or move the auth-mount tune and role creation into a dedicated fixture with teardown.
